name: NotebookLM: Add YouTube Source
plan_guidance:
KNOWN SKILL: NotebookLM YouTube Source Ingestion

NotebookLM is a WEB APP in Chrome. Use the browser action "click" (Chrome Bridge DOM matching)
for EVERY click in this skill — NEVER use "click_screen" (native pixel click). click_screen
picks up the wrong element on NotebookLM (featured-notebook tiles visible on the page can steal
the click), while Chrome Bridge "click" matches the DOM accessibility name exactly.

Follow this EXACT sequence. Do NOT invent variants.

  1. navigate → https://notebooklm.google.com/
  2. click    → "Create new notebook"            (URL changes to /notebook/<UUID>)
  3. click    → "Add source"                     (modal opens, URL gains ?addSource=true)
  4. click    → "YouTube"                        (NOT the "Web" tab, NOT "Paste text")
  5. type     → <full YouTube URL>
  6. click    → "Insert"                         (modal closes, URL loses ?addSource=true)
  7. wait     → 30                                (NotebookLM processes the video)
  8. click    → the source title as shown in the modal preview or URL slug — use Chrome Bridge
                "click" and pass the EXACT text you saw when the source was first added, NOT
                any other title visible on the page (featured notebooks have lookalike titles).
  9. read_screen                                  (summary text is in the main panel)

CRITICAL PITFALLS:
- After step 6 "Insert", the page text may STILL read "0 sources, Saved sources will appear here"
  for 5–30 seconds. This is NOT proof that Insert failed. ALWAYS wait:30 before re-reading.
- Do NOT click "Add source" or "Insert" multiple times in a row. One Insert is enough.
- Do NOT create a new notebook if the current URL already contains "/notebook/<UUID>".
- The modal's submit button is labeled "Insert" — NOT "Add", NOT "Create", NOT "Submit".
- NEVER click Cancel / Close / X / Discard on the Add Source modal — that throws away the URL.
- The YouTube tile's DOM element-text may appear as "video_youtube" (an icon name); clicking
  "YouTube" label is what works.
- NotebookLM's home/featured area lists other notebooks with titles like "Incremental
  Construction", "Can a computer simulate a brain?", etc. DO NOT click these — they are not
  your added source. Only click titles that match the YouTube video you just added.
react_guidance:
NOTEBOOKLM SKILL ACTIVE — Add-YouTube workflow. Use Chrome Bridge "click" for all clicks — NEVER "click_screen".
Order: Create notebook → Add source → YouTube → type URL → Insert → wait 30s → click YOUR source title.
If URL contains "?addSource=true" the modal is open: type the URL then click "Insert".
If the source panel says "0 sources" LESS THAN 30 seconds after clicking Insert, do NOT re-click
Insert — use wait:30. NotebookLM's React UI updates lazily.
When clicking a source title in step 8, avoid featured-notebook titles (MoE models, brain
simulation, etc.) — click only the title matching the YouTube URL you just added.

name: Facebook: Compose and Publish Post
intent: compose and publish a facebook post
plan_guidance:
KNOWN SKILL: Facebook Compose-and-Publish

Facebook is a WEB APP in Chrome. Use the browser action "click" (Chrome Bridge DOM) for every
click in this skill — NEVER "click_screen". Chrome Bridge matches DOM accessibility names and
is dramatically more reliable on Facebook's complex React UI than pixel-based native clicks.

Sequence:
  1. navigate → https://www.facebook.com/
  2. click    → "What's on your mind"           (OPENS A MODAL DIALOG, not an inline input)
  3. wait     → 2                                (modal transition)
  4. read_screen                                  (verify modal opened)
  5. click    → the modal's text area            (use Chrome Bridge "click", NOT click_screen)
  6. type     → the post content (multi-line, multi-language supported)
  7. click    → "Post"                           (publishes and closes modal)
  8. read_screen                                  (verify post appears in feed)

CRITICAL PITFALLS:
- Facebook's composer is a MODAL, not the inline placeholder. After clicking
  "What's on your mind", a full-screen dialog opens. Type into the MODAL.
- NEVER click Close, Cancel, Discard, Dismiss, Exit, or X on the composer — that throws away
  your draft. The pre-discard guard will block this, but you should not attempt it.
- The publish button is labeled "Post" (not "Publish", not "Share", not "Send").
- If "Post" appears disabled after typing, click the modal body once more to refocus the input,
  then try "Post" again.
- The composer auto-generates link previews. Posting a YouTube URL produces a thumbnail card —
  this is normal, do NOT click away to dismiss it.
- After successfully clicking "Post" ONCE, do NOT click "Post" again. The modal closes and the
  button is no longer bound to your draft. Subsequent clicks will be on an empty composer or
  an unrelated "Post" button elsewhere on the page — they won't duplicate publish but will
  waste budget. If read_screen shows the Facebook feed (news stories, posts, etc.) the post
  was published — consider the goal done.
react_guidance:
FACEBOOK SKILL ACTIVE — compose flow. Use Chrome Bridge "click" (not "click_screen") for all clicks.
To post: click "What's on your mind" → MODAL opens → type in modal → click "Post" ONCE.
NEVER click Close / Cancel / Discard / X — the pre-discard guard blocks these and you lose the draft.
Only "Post" publishes. After ONE successful "Post" click, stop clicking Post — the modal closes
and further clicks are wasted. If you see the feed (news stories, posts), the goal is DONE.

name: Facebook: Edit Existing Post
plan_guidance:
KNOWN SKILL: Facebook Edit Existing Post

Facebook is a WEB APP in Chrome. Use the browser action "click" (Chrome Bridge DOM) for every
click in this skill — NEVER "click_screen". Chrome Bridge matches DOM accessibility names and
is dramatically more reliable on Facebook's React UI than pixel-based native clicks.

The goal will reference a specific post, usually by a text prefix/snippet (e.g. "the post
starting with 'Hôm nay mình vừa khám phá...'"). Your job is to LOCATE that post, open its
edit modal, modify its text, and save.

Sequence:
  1. navigate    → https://www.facebook.com/me                (goes to the USER's own profile —
                                                               the home feed shows other people's
                                                               posts, NOT the user's. Editing
                                                               requires being on your own profile
                                                               or the individual post's permalink.)
  2. wait        → 2                                           (profile timeline loads)
  3. read_screen                                               (see the most-recent posts)
  4. If the target post prefix/snippet is NOT visible in read_screen text:
       scroll → down  ;  wait → 1  ;  read_screen
     Emit AT MOST 3 such scroll-wait-read cycles in the plan (6 on the profile timeline
     is plenty to reach posts from the last few weeks; more scroll cycles just bloat the
     plan and leave no budget for the click/type/Save steps that actually land the edit).
     The REACT loop will bail out of these cycles early as soon as read_screen shows the
     target post, so additional cycles are wasted plan budget, not safety margin.

     Match by PREFIX / SUBSTRING, not exact full text — Facebook truncates long posts with
     "See more" in the feed, so only the first ~200–400 chars are present in the DOM.
     Non-ASCII (Vietnamese, emoji) IS preserved in read_screen output.

     ⚠️  DO NOT click the post title or body text to "open" it — that navigates to the post
     permalink page (URL /posts/pfbid…) and makes the three-dot menu HARDER to target, not
     easier. Stay on the profile/timeline view.

  5. Open the three-dot "…" menu on the target post. USE click_scoped FOR THIS STEP.

     ★ Why click_scoped, not click ★
     Every post on the profile has its own three-dot menu, and ALL of them share the
     same aria-label ("Actions for this post"). Plain `click` hits the first DOM match,
     which is whatever post appears first in the feed — NOT necessarily the target.
     click_scoped anchors on the target post's unique text prefix, walks UP to the post
     container, then walks DOWN to the three-dot button inside THAT container. Result:
     the correct post's menu opens, guaranteed.

     Emit the step as:
       action: click_scoped
       anchor: <the first 30–60 chars of the target post — use the prefix from the goal,
                e.g. "Hôm nay mình vừa khám phá một cách làm việc với AI">
       target: "Actions for this post"  (English aria-label — Facebook keeps this in
                                          English even on Vietnamese UI. DO NOT translate.)

     If "Actions for this post" fails, retry with target="More options for this post"
     (older variant). Vietnamese targets ("Tùy chọn khác cho bài viết này") work only
     on some A/B arms — use as a last resort.

     After the click, wait → 1, then read_screen to verify the menu opened (you should
     see "Edit post" / "Chỉnh sửa bài viết" in the output). If not visible, the click
     landed on the wrong element; retry with the next target candidate above.

  6. Click the Edit option in the popup menu — use plain `click`, NOT click_scoped.

     ★ Why plain click, not click_scoped ★
     Facebook renders popup menus (and modal dialogs) in REACT PORTALS — they mount
     at document.body root, NOT as descendants of the post. click_scoped walks UP
     from the post prefix and DOWN through that ancestor's subtree; menu options
     in a portal are outside that subtree, so click_scoped will fail with "no
     ancestor contained 'Edit post'". Plain `click` searches globally by aria-label
     and will hit the open menu's option correctly — only ONE menu is rendered at
     a time, so there's no disambiguation problem here.

     Emit as:
       action: click
       target: "Edit post"   (English aria-label — Facebook keeps this in English
                               on Vietnamese UI too)

     Fallback targets if "Edit post" fails: "Edit Post" (title-case), then
     "Chỉnh sửa bài viết" (Vietnamese last-resort).

     After clicking, read_screen to verify the edit modal opened — it shows the
     current post text in a textarea plus a "Save" / "Lưu" button. If the modal
     isn't visible, step 5 hit the wrong menu — do NOT proceed to typing. Use
     action=failed instead.

     THE PORTAL RULE: any step that targets content inside a popup/dialog/menu
     that opened as a result of a previous click should use plain `click`, not
     click_scoped. Only use click_scoped for controls that are rendered inline
     within a list of look-alike siblings (like the three-dot menu in step 5).
  7. wait → 2                                                  (edit modal opens)
  8. read_screen                                               (verify edit composer is open;
                                                               you should see the CURRENT
                                                               post text in a textarea, plus
                                                               a "Save" or "Lưu" button.
                                                               If NOT, step 6 clicked the
                                                               wrong thing — go back to 5a.)
  9. Determine the NEW post content now, BEFORE typing. Use the post text you just read in
     step 8 as the basis. Apply the transformation the goal requested (strip markdown, add
     URLs, etc.). Preserve every word of the original content unless the goal explicitly
     says to remove it.
 10. type → the NEW post content

     ★ DO NOT emit a separate key_press cmd+a step before type ★
     The Chrome Bridge type_text handler ALREADY does select-all + replace internally.
     It finds the contenteditable editor inside the [role="dialog"] modal, focuses it,
     selects all existing content via DOM range selection, deletes it, then inserts the
     new text. Adding a native cmd+a before this BREAKS the flow: the native keystroke
     steals focus to the URL bar or page body, and then Chrome Bridge types into the
     wrong element.

     Also DO NOT emit a separate "click the textarea" step before type.
     Chrome Bridge type_text auto-discovers and focuses the editor.

 11. click → "Save" (English) or "Lưu" (Vietnamese)
 14. wait → 2                                                  (modal closes, post updates)
 15. read_screen                                               (verify the edit landed — the
                                                               post text on the profile should
                                                               now start with the new content)

CRITICAL PITFALLS:
- The home feed (facebook.com/) does NOT show your own posts reliably. ALWAYS start at
  facebook.com/me for edit flows.
- NEVER use the post's own title/body text as a click target when you mean to click the
  three-dot menu. Chrome Bridge DOM matching will pick the big post-text region and your
  menu-open step will silently no-op. The menu button has a DISTINCT accessibility name —
  use read_page (step 5a) to discover it.
- If step 5c seems to succeed (click returned ok) but step 5e's read_screen shows no
  "Edit post" / "Chỉnh sửa bài viết" option, the menu did NOT actually open. Do NOT proceed
  to step 6 — loop back to 5a and try a different menu-button name from the 5b list.
- Matching post prefix by EXACT full text is brittle. Use 30–80 chars from the beginning.
- Vietnamese diacritics and emoji MUST be preserved byte-for-byte when typing new content.
- NEVER click "Delete post", "Xóa bài viết", "Move to trash", "Hide from profile", "Hide
  from timeline" on the popup menu — destructive, blocked by the pre-discard guard.
- The save button in the EDIT modal is "Save" / "Lưu" — NOT "Post" (that's the compose modal)
  and NOT "Update".
- Do NOT click "Cancel", "Discard", "Hủy", "Bỏ", or X on the edit modal — that throws away
  your edit.
- If after 8 scrolls the target post prefix is not found, STOP and report the goal as
  blocked — do NOT guess at a different post.
- If after 3 attempts at step 5 the menu still won't open, STOP and report blocked — do NOT
  start clicking on the post text as a desperate fallback, that just navigates you into the
  permalink page and wastes the remaining action budget.
react_guidance:
FACEBOOK SKILL ACTIVE — edit-existing-post. Use Chrome Bridge, never click_screen.
Start at facebook.com/me. Scroll + read_screen to find target post by PREFIX (30–80 chars).

★ click_scoped vs click — THE PORTAL RULE ★
Use click_scoped ONLY for the three-dot menu trigger (every post on the profile has its
own "Actions for this post" trigger rendered INLINE — plain click hits the wrong one).
Emit click_scoped as:
  ACTION: click_scoped
  ANCHOR: <target post's first 30-60 chars, taken from the goal's quoted prefix>
  TARGET: <aria-label of the trigger, e.g. "Actions for this post">

Use PLAIN click for everything that appears AFTER a menu/dialog opens (Edit post option,
text area inside the edit modal, Save/Lưu button). Those are rendered in REACT PORTALS
at document.body root — they are NOT descendants of the post. click_scoped would fail
with "no ancestor contained <target>". Plain click searches globally by aria-label and
works correctly because only ONE menu/modal is open at a time, so first-match is right.

★ FB KEEPS ARIA-LABELS IN ENGLISH on Vietnamese UI ★
Try English FIRST, Vietnamese only as last resort:
  Three-dot menu:  "Actions for this post"   →  "More options for this post"  →  "Tùy chọn khác cho bài viết này"
  Edit option:     "Edit post"                →  "Edit Post"                    →  "Chỉnh sửa bài viết"
  Text area:       "What's on your mind"      →  (compose textarea)             →  "Bạn đang nghĩ gì"
  Save button:     "Save"                     →                                  →  "Lưu"

★ TYPE REPLACES — NO CMD+A NEEDED ★
Chrome Bridge type_text auto-finds the dialog editor, selects all, replaces. Do NOT
emit key_press cmd+a or click on the textarea as separate steps before type. Those
steal focus and cause duplication. Just emit: ACTION: type / TARGET: <new content>.

★ HARD-STOP RULES ★
- NEVER click Cancel / Discard / Hủy / Bỏ / X on the edit modal.
- NEVER click Delete / Xóa / Hide / Trash.
- NEVER use the post's own body text as a fallback click target.
- If the Edit-post click fails OR the edit modal isn't visible in read_screen after 2
  attempts, STOP with ACTION: failed. Do NOT proceed to type / Save — typing into the
  wrong element corrupts unrelated fields.
- If type happened but the edit modal isn't visible, do NOT click Save.
